quests.sentence: All museum visitors must not touch any of the artwork.
quests.hint: 'Must not' shows something is forbidden, followed by the base verb.
quests.explanation: Must not touch expresses a strict prohibition, using must not plus the base form of the verb.

quests.sentence: Delivery drivers cannot park directly in front of the entrance.
quests.hint: 'Cannot' shows something is not allowed, followed by the base verb park.
quests.explanation: Cannot park expresses a rule against an action, using cannot plus the base form of the verb.

quests.sentence: All company employees cannot share confidential client information with anyone.
quests.hint: 'Cannot' is followed directly by the base verb share.
quests.explanation: Cannot share expresses a firm rule against an action, using cannot plus the base form of the verb.

quests.sentence: Plain water always boils quickly if you heat it enough.
quests.hint: Zero conditional uses present tense in both parts; put the main clause first to avoid a comma.
quests.explanation: If you heat it enough describes a general truth, and both clauses use the simple present tense.

quests.sentence: Fresh ice always melts quickly if you leave it outside.
quests.hint: Both parts of a zero conditional use the simple present tense.
quests.explanation: Melts quickly and if you leave it outside both use present tense, showing a general scientific fact.

quests.sentence: Most garden plants grow faster if they get enough sunlight.
quests.hint: The main clause comes first, then 'if' plus the condition, both in present tense.
quests.explanation: Grow faster and if they get enough sunlight both use present tense, describing a general truth about plants.

quests.sentence: The support team responded quickly to the client complaint yesterday.
quests.hint: Manner (quickly) comes first, then the object phrase, then the time word.
quests.explanation: Responded quickly (manner) is followed by to the client complaint (object phrase) and yesterday (time).

quests.sentence: City engineers tested the new bridge design carefully last month.
quests.hint: Manner (carefully) follows the object, and time (last month) comes at the very end.
quests.explanation: Tested the bridge design carefully (manner) is followed by last month (time), the standard closing order.

quests.sentence: Local volunteers cleaned the entire riverbank thoroughly early this morning.
quests.hint: Manner (thoroughly) comes right after the object, then the time phrase at the end.
quests.explanation: Cleaned the riverbank thoroughly (manner) is followed by early this morning (time), the natural closing order.

quests.sentence: Please fill in all your personal details on this form.
quests.hint: 'Fill in' can stay together before a longer noun object.
quests.explanation: Fill in all your details keeps the phrasal verb together, since the object is a fairly long noun phrase.

quests.sentence: She looked the strange new word up in a dictionary.
quests.hint: With a short noun object, the particle 'up' can follow the object.
quests.explanation: Looked the word up splits the phrasal verb look up, placing the object between the verb and the particle.

quests.sentence: I really need you to set this printer up correctly.
quests.hint: The object (this printer) can go between 'set' and 'up'.
quests.explanation: Set this printer up splits the phrasal verb set up, placing the object between the verb and the particle.

quests.sentence: You should probably see a dentist at least twice a year.
quests.hint: 'Should' gives advice, followed by the base verb, then the frequency phrase.
quests.explanation: Should probably see gives cautious advice, followed by the frequency phrase at least twice a year.

quests.sentence: Local residents ought to report broken streetlights to the city.
quests.hint: 'Ought to' works like 'should', followed by the base verb report.
quests.explanation: Ought to report gives strong advice, using ought to plus the base verb, followed by the object and receiver.

quests.sentence: You should probably rest well after such a long flight.
quests.hint: 'Should' is followed by an adverb of likelihood, then the base verb.
quests.explanation: Should probably rest gives cautious advice, with probably placed between should and the base verb rest.

quests.sentence: Our connecting flight will finally depart from gate twelve shortly.
quests.hint: 'Will' is followed directly by the base verb depart, then the place.
quests.explanation: Will finally depart shows a scheduled future event, followed by the place from gate twelve.

quests.sentence: We are definitely going to relocate our office next quarter.
quests.hint: 'Going to' shows a decided plan, followed by the base verb relocate.
quests.explanation: Are definitely going to relocate shows a firm future plan, using be + going to + base verb.

quests.sentence: The regional manager will finally announce the results this afternoon.
quests.hint: 'Will' is followed by an adverb and then the base verb announce.
quests.explanation: Will finally announce shows a confident future prediction, with finally placed between will and the base verb.

quests.sentence: Most people feel much healthier if they sleep enough hours.
quests.hint: Zero conditional uses present tense throughout to state a general truth.
quests.explanation: Feel much healthier and if they sleep enough hours both use present tense, expressing a general truth about health.

quests.sentence: Fresh bread turns moldy if you leave it too long.
quests.hint: Notice how both the result and the condition stay in the simple present tense throughout.
quests.explanation: Turns moldy and if you leave it too long both use present tense, describing a general, predictable outcome.

quests.sentence: Most solid metal expands slightly if you heat it directly.
quests.hint: Both the main clause and the if-clause use the simple present tense.
quests.explanation: Expands slightly and if you heat it directly both use present tense, showing a scientific general truth.

quests.sentence: All foreign tourists must carry valid identification at all times.
quests.hint: 'Must' is followed by the base verb carry, then the object.
quests.explanation: Must carry expresses a strict requirement, using must plus the base verb, followed by the object and time phrase.

quests.sentence: All job applicants have to complete the online form fully.
quests.hint: 'Have to' functions like 'must', followed by the base verb complete.
quests.explanation: Have to complete expresses a necessary step, using have to plus the base verb, followed by the object.

quests.sentence: All city drivers must stop completely at every red light.
quests.hint: 'Must' is followed by the base verb, then an adverb, then the place.
quests.explanation: Must stop completely expresses a strict traffic rule, using must plus the base verb and a following adverb.

quests.sentence: Our family gathered happily at the beach house last summer.
quests.hint: Manner (happily) comes first, then place (at the beach house), then time (last summer).
quests.explanation: Gathered happily (manner) is followed by at the beach house (place) and last summer (time), the standard order.

quests.sentence: The school choir performed beautifully at the concert hall Saturday.
quests.hint: Manner comes right after the verb, then place, then the day at the end.
quests.explanation: Performed beautifully (manner) is followed by at the concert hall (place) and Saturday (time).

quests.sentence: Our friendly neighbors chatted warmly on the porch every evening.
quests.hint: Manner (warmly) follows the verb, then place (on the porch), then the frequency phrase.
quests.explanation: Chatted warmly (manner) is followed by on the porch (place) and every evening (frequency), the usual order.

quests.sentence: Water always boils faster if you add a little salt.
quests.hint: Combine the zero conditional with a comparative adverb in one sentence.
quests.explanation: This review sentence mixes the zero conditional (if you add salt) with a comparative form (faster).

quests.sentence: All office employees must fill in their weekly timesheets accurately.
quests.hint: Combine modal necessity with a phrasal verb and a manner adverb.
quests.explanation: This checkpoint mixes modal necessity (must fill in) with a phrasal verb and a closing manner adverb.

quests.sentence: Our whole family will gather happily at the lake next summer.
quests.hint: Combine future simple with manner, place, and time adverbials.
quests.explanation: This review sentence brings together future simple (will gather) with manner, place, and time in one sentence.
